svg.title: ADBC logomark isometric construction grid
svg.text: Isometric projection, on the hex badge’s triangle grid. Every edge lands on a grid line, and the X comes from whole cells.
top front wall + bottom back wall
Equilateral triangles: grid lines run three ways, vertical and ±30°, all
equally spaced. True isometric: view angle = arcsin(1/√3) ≈ 35.26°.
11 × 11 cells. Hole 9 × 9 (82%). Rim 1 cell all round.
Wall 2 cells tall, gap 3, so each layer sits 5 below the last.
Square 11 = rim 1 + two pitches of 5, so the top layer’s front walls land on the
same grid lines as the bottom layer’s back walls. Each pair reads as one band.
Down the axis: rim 1, wall 2, space 2, every 5 cells (one pitch), for 23.
Every wall, front or back, falls on this beat; the X is where two coincide.
Gap 3 = rim 1 + wall 2, so each tab is 2 × 2: the same as the X’s
crossing and each of its short lower arms.
11 wide × 23 tall. The top cell is white rim, so the ink is 11 × 22:
11√3 : 22 = √3 : 2, exactly the box of a regular hexagon.
